title: What is Debugging?
description: Debugging is the systematic process of identifying, analyzing, and resolving bugs or defects in software to ensure it functions as intended.
solution:
1. Isolate the faulty code.
2. Reproduce the bug.
3. Analyze state using logs or debuggers.
4. Fix and verify.
tip: Always tackle one bug at a time to avoid complex side effects.

title: Undefined is not a function
description: This occurs when you attempt to call a value as a function, but that value is undefined. Usually due to missing imports or scope issues.
solution: Check if the function exists before calling it or ensure it's properly assigned.
tip: Use optional chaining: obj.calculate?.() to prevent crashes.

title: 404 Not Found vs 500 Server Error
description: 404 means the endpoint doesn't exist (client error). 500 means the server crashed while processing the request (backend error).
solution: For 404: Check URL spelling. For 500: Check backend logs and database connectivity.
tip: Always implement global error boundaries in your API services.

title: The Overflow Nightmare
description: Content leaking out of its container usually happens when fixed widths are used or flexbox properties aren't constrained.
solution: Use overflow: hidden or max-width: 100% to contain child elements.
tip: Use 'overflow-x: hidden' on the body tag as a safety net for mobile layouts.

title: The Missing 'await' Trap
description: Forgetting 'await' before a promise returns the Promise object instead of the resolved data, leading to unexpected 'Promise <pending>' values.
solution: Always use await: const data = await fetchUser();
tip: Use try/catch blocks with async functions to handle rejected promises gracefully.

title: Unit Testing 101
description: Unit tests focus on testing individual components or functions in isolation from the rest of the app.
solution: Write tests that cover edge cases, not just the happy path.
tip: Good tests should be independent, fast, and repeatable.

title: Chrome DevTools: Network Tab
description: The Network tab is your eyes into the communication between your app and the server.
example: // Filter by 'Fetch/XHR' to see API calls
solution: Inspect headers, payloads, and response status codes to find API bottlenecks.
tip: Use 'Throttling' to simulate slow 3G connections and test loading states.

title: Rubber Duck Debugging
description: Explain your problem out loud to an inanimate object. Translating the problem into words often exposes the logical flaw in your approach.
solution:
1. Step away from typing.
2. Explain the code line-by-line.
3. Notice the incorrect assumptions.
tip: Writing the problem down in a notebook has a similar cognitive effect.

title: Isolate the Bug
description: Remove layers of complexity. Create a minimal reproducible example (MRE). If the bug disappears, the issue is in the removed code.
solution:
1. Comment out unrelated code.
2. Hardcode variables to bypass external factors.
3. Test the broken logic in isolation.
tip: Codepen or CodeSandbox are great for building minimal reproducible examples.

title: Use Version Control (Git Bisect)
description: If a bug suddenly appears, use git bisect to find the exact commit that introduced the problem by performing a binary search on the history.
example:
$ git bisect start
$ git bisect bad HEAD
$ git bisect good v1.2.0
# Git checks out a midpoint for you to test.
solution:
1. Find a known good state.
2. Narrow down the offending commit.
3. Review the diff to understand what broke.
tip: Keep commits small and focused so identifying the root cause is easier.

title: 200 OK
description: The standard response for successful HTTP requests. It means the request was received, understood, and processed successfully.
solution: No action needed. Ensure your client correctly parses the returned data substrate.
tip: The most common success code. Use it for GET, PUT, and successful POST requests.

title: 201 Created
description: Indicates that the request has been fulfilled and has resulted in one or more new resources being created on the server.
solution: Verify the resource was successfully created in the database and provide its URI in the Location header.
tip: Best practice for RESTful APIs when creating new entities via POST.

title: 204 No Content
description: The server successfully processed the request, but is not returning any content in the response body.
solution: Use this when a confirmation of success is needed but no data return is required.
tip: Commonly used for successful DELETE or PUT requests that don't need a response body.

title: 301 Moved Permanently
description: The requested resource has been assigned a new permanent URI. Future references should use one of the returned URIs.
solution: Update internal links and ensure the 'Location' header points to the correct destination.
tip: Essential for SEO to preserve link authority during URL migrations.

title: 304 Not Modified
description: Indicates that the resource has not been modified since the version specified by the request headers If-Modified-Since or If-None-Match.
example:
GET /static/style.css HTTP/1.1
If-None-Match: "v1.2"

HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
solution: Client should use its cached version of the resource. No body is sent.
tip: Reduces bandwidth usage and improves performance through neural caching.

title: 400 Bad Request
description: The server cannot process the request due to a client error (e.g., malformed request syntax, invalid request message framing).
solution: Validate request payloads on the client side. Ensure the content-type matches the payload.
tip: Often points to a mismatch between frontend state and backend validation schemas.

title: 401 Unauthorized
description: Semantically this means 'unauthenticated'. The client must authenticate itself to get the requested response.
solution: Redirect to login or trigger a token refresh flow. Check if the Bearer token is expired.
tip: Always check the 'WWW-Authenticate' header for details on the required authentication.

title: 403 Forbidden
description: The client does not have access rights to the content. Unlike 401, the client's identity is known to the server.
example:
GET /api/admin-core HTTP/1.1
(User has 'member' role only)

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
solution: Verify user permissions and role-based access controls (RBAC). Ensure the user has the required scopes.
tip: Often used to block unwanted neural probes or restricted administrative logic.

title: 404 Not Found
description: The server cannot find the requested resource. This can also be used to hide the existence of a resource from an unauthorized client.
solution: Check URL spelling, dynamic route parameters, and verify the resource exists in the database.
tip: Dead links are toxic to user experience and SEO. Use audits to find them.

title: 405 Method Not Allowed
description: The request method is known by the server but is not supported by the target resource.
example:
POST /api/static-file HTTP/1.1

HTTP/1.1 405 Method Not Allowed
Allow: GET, HEAD
solution: Check your API documentation. Use the correct HTTP verb (GET, POST, etc.) for the endpoint.
tip: Check the 'Allow' header in the response to see which methods are permitted.

title: 422 Unprocessable Entity
description: The request was well-formed but was unable to be followed due to semantic errors (e.g., validation failed).
solution: Correct the validation errors reported in the server's response body.
tip: Standard for modern JSON APIs to communicate complex validation failures.

title: 429 Too Many Requests
description: The user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time ('rate limiting').
solution: Implement exponential backoff or wait for the 'Retry-After' duration before re-syncing.
tip: Critical for protecting neural substrates from DDoS or abusive scraping.

title: 500 Internal Server Error
description: General error message when an unexpected condition was encountered and no more specific message is suitable.
example:
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error

{ "error": "Neural Bridge Failure (NullPointer)" }
solution: Check backend logs immediately. This usually indicates a crash in the server-side logic.
tip: The 'catch-all' of server errors. Always monitor for spikes in 500s.

title: 502 Bad Gateway
description: The server, while acting as a gateway or proxy, received an invalid response from the upstream server.
solution: Check the status of upstream microservices or reverse proxies (like Nginx/Cloudflare).
tip: Often points to a communication failure between different parts of the infrastructure.

title: 503 Service Unavailable
description: The server is currently unable to handle the request due to a temporary overload or scheduled maintenance.
solution: Check server load, horizontal scaling status, or maintenance windows.
tip: Use this code to signal clients that they should try again later.

title: 504 Gateway Timeout
description: The server, while acting as a gateway or proxy, did not receive a timely response from the upstream server.
solution: Increase timeout thresholds or optimize the performance of the upstream neural process.
tip: Common when long-running tasks (like deep scans) exceed proxy timeouts.
